note: For each domain: the eight steps of the workflow and the performing and ownership conditions for the eight judgment axes. Items, the results report and experience input all read this one file. `verify_targets` and `artifacts` are what the results report's action steps draw on, so they must be concrete here to avoid vague wording

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Work arrives that must first answer what to make and whom to show it to

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: What the advertiser or planner said, audience data, records of past episodes, available time and money

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: What to communicate, the audience, and the range of cases to look at

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Asking and collecting, grouping, narrowing down, and narrowing again if it was wrong

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Audience research forms, case storage tools, records of past episodes, media data, interview question lists

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: A plan, one page about the audience, a case summary, dropped topics and the reasons

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: What the audience says, similar cases, what the advertiser wants, the response after release

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If the plan is called off the point, separate whether the message was chosen wrongly or the audience was read wrongly

J1.l2: Wrote down separately what to communicate this time and what not to communicate
J1.l3: The range I set became the scope of that task

J2.l2: Turned what the advertiser said into items that can be checked
J2.l3: The items I wrote became the agreed criteria of that task

J3.l2: When there were several audiences, decided myself which one to look at first
J3.l3: The plan settled in the direction I decided

J4.l2: Chose and applied a research method and a range of data to collect
J4.l3: The method I chose became the team's basic research

J5.l2: Kept a plan and research records
J5.l3: Another person started production with the plan I left

J6.l2: Checked the plan against what the audience said or similar cases
J6.l3: Changed the message or the audience based on the check

J7.l2: Narrowed the reason it was called off the point down to the message or the audience
J7.l3: Changed the plan and confirmed an improvement in the next episode

J8.l2: The planning method I built became the team's starting template
J8.l3: My research results were used in the advertiser's decision

org_outcomes.OC4: Defining tasks for corporate public relations

domains.name: Message and Concept

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Work arrives that must decide how to say this task in one line

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: The plan and research results, the impression the advertiser wants, the words the brand already uses, time and people

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: The one line to say, what to keep and what to drop

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Writing several options, having people read them, narrowing to one, explaining and fixing

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Message templates, collections of example copy, presentation tools, copy review forms, reading response records

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: One line of message, one page on the tone, what to keep and drop, dropped messages and the reasons

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: The plan, the words the brand already uses, readers' responses, results after release

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If the copy is called ordinary, separate whether the message is too broad or has no evidence

artifacts: List of expressions to use and expressions to avoid

domains.name: Media and Channel Planning

workflow.name: Inputs received

workflow.name: Deliverables produced

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Reach data for each media channel, results of past episodes, available money, numbers after release

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: If it is said not to reach people, separate whether the media channel, the amount or the material is the cause

review_note: Media, advertising and performance majors release work at a set place on a set day, so **if no record remains, the judgments of that day disappear.** What keeps the domains apart is `required_axes`. Message, shooting, directing, directing performers, public relations and crisis, and rights and review depend on outputs: a one-page concept, a shooting plan, a script, directions, a press release and check records must remain so that the next person can take over. Planning, media, sound, and rights and review depend on comparison and verification: the task set, the media chosen, the sound mixed and the rights checked are **not evidence until they are checked against standards, past episodes or review specifications.** Editing, on-site work and results measurement depend on failure and correction: it is common for things not to connect or fit at first, and narrowing down the reason is the work. Media and public relations and crisis depend on interpreting requirements: if the given goals and confirmed facts are not turned into conditions, nothing can be released. So even if six axes are confirmed, the evidence does not hold when a required axis of that domain is empty
